A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Just Pass Twice (JPT). Their complete main texts, Appendices A–G, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original JPT benchmark results, efficiency measurements, ablations, attention visualizations, and error analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds a generative-backbone comparison and single-input failure examples in Appendix E.

M1.justification: Input duplication, definition injection through prompts and embeddings, projection layers, LoRA adaptation, classification, losses, and inference remain unchanged, including the dual-head implementation already documented in Appendix A.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Wikipedia-derived training corpus, CrossNER and MIT benchmarks, extended 20-dataset suite, and private evaluation set. The added backbone comparison and single-input examples examine retained NER coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds standalone generative Qwen3-4B as a comparator to JPT-4B on CrossNER in Appendix E.3 and Table 11. Comparator membership in the existing benchmark and efficiency tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix E.3 adds a comparison controlling backbone identity and size, evaluating base Qwen3-4B generatively with the NER prompt from Ye et al. Existing evaluation settings remain unchanged. The clarification that ablation variants were separately trained documents their setup rather than establishing a revised protocol.

E4.justification: Appendix E adds a backbone comparison examining the complete framework's contribution and four single-input failure cases involving early-mention type confusion or missed entities. Existing duplication, definition, model-size, LoRA-rank, attention, and full-model error analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the experimental results. The added related-work discussion of uncertainty estimation does not introduce statistical analysis of JPT.

E6.justification: v3 Table 11 adds Qwen3-4B results averaging 57.4 F1 versus 74.4 for JPT-4B across five CrossNER domains, a 17.0-point gap. JPT's domain scores match v1; this is an added comparison, not improved JPT performance. Table 12 also adds four qualitative failure results.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5, the causal-attention coverage argument, classification definitions, and complexity discussion are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: duplication enables contextual token classification, definitions support zero-shot typing, and JPT achieves the reported 7.9-point advantage and over 20-fold speedup. Added evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix E.3 newly attributes the backbone-comparison gap primarily to the JPT framework. E.4 interprets single-input failures through unavailable future context and explains why separate training avoids a training–inference mismatch. The existing limitations and full-model error interpretations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendix E.4 clarify that ablation variants were fine-tuned separately, particularly that single-input evaluation does not merely disable duplication at inference. The project-page address changes from the WitnessAI site to an hf.space address; code and weights remain described as forthcoming.

R1.justification: v3 adds six references and Section 2.3 on input duplication and multi-prompt inference. The introduction and related work explicitly distinguish Springer et al.'s pooled retrieval embeddings from JPT's individual token representations. Existing NER-related positioning is retained.

P1.justification: Changes comprise a localized introduction revision, an added related-work subsection, clearer ablation explanations, and two additional appendix subsections. Most existing prose and the overall document organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 11 and 12 and relocates existing displays as text reflows. The former Tables 11 and 12 become Tables 13 and 14. Existing figure content, plot axes, and established table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 better acknowledges relevant duplication research, clarifies how ablations were trained, and adds a useful backbone comparison and concrete single-input failures. These modestly strengthen clarity and empirical support. The new comparison evaluates the combined trained framework, however, so it does not isolate individual components as strongly as the causal interpretation in Appendix E.3 suggests.
